Change has been successfully rebased and submitted as 608ad2cc0e17bf62ff34bae7ceb499816fe13fbb
It looks good, after the rebase is done.
I rebased to resolve the merge conflict

> With this, the accidental copy by doing lambda capture can be prevented. This is good.
> 
> However, it makes also difficult to do the lambda capture (not for the purpose of copy).
> 
> 
> Previously it can be done like
> ```
>      [req, ...]() {    
>           // access via req. 
>      }
>     or, 
>      [req=std::move(req.copy(), ...](){ }
> ```
> 
> This wouldn't work.

Right....  That is roughly the point of this patch.  We should never really be capturing a full request in an async callback.  We know the structures that exist, it should not require IO to be able to parse a request to a more specific data structure.

> 
> 
> So, after this, to capture, it needs to create a shared_ptr<> to hold the copy of it.
> ```
>      [req=std::make_shared<Request&>(req.copy(), ...]()
>      {  
>         // access via req-> 
>      }
> ```
> 
> 
> OR 
> https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/78759 can make the lambda capture easier without duplicating it.
> 
> ```
>      [req{req.shared_from_this()}, ...]()
>      {  
>         // access via req-> 
>      }
> ```

or

[req = req.copy()] ()....

I'd also point out, it's intentional that we make this harder.  I see a large number of patches that make copies.  Even in our own code we have a few places where we make request copies that I didn't catch.  Every one of them is an opportunity to reduce our peak memory usage.

Understood and agreed -- about "intentional that we make this harder".

However, my question is how can we capture it if needed (for the purpose of the lifetime of the request, not necessary for the copy) ?  With this copy() approach, the only way is to create a copy of it and make it as shared_ptr.

> Understood and agreed -- about "intentional that we make this harder".
> 
> However, my question is how can we capture it if needed (for the purpose of the lifetime of the request, not necessary for the copy) ?

When would that be needed?  The current lifetime of the request is however long the first callback handler lasts.  Once it's done, request is burned.

So I think the answer to your question is that you'd just pass by reference in the first caller.  If you want to CHANGE the lifetime, that's a different question.

>  With this copy() approach, the only way is to create a copy of it and make it as shared_ptr.
Myung,
does this answer your question?  I'm happy to chat more in another forum about this, and if there's changes needed, please let me know.

Ed,

Unfortunately, this does not work
`[req = req.copy()] ()....`

It is because
```
operator=(const Request&) = delete
private:L Request(const Request& other) = default;
```

Then, the method that I can think of is
```
     [req=std::make_shared<Request&>(req.copy(), ...]()
     {  
        // access via req-> 
     }
```

It may look like a little awkward, but overall, I think this commit seems still better as we can prevent the undesired copy.

If you agree it, let merge this.

[req(req.copy())] ()

is what I would expect to work.
n my experiment, it does not work as the matching constructor is private.

The error I see when I try that is that std::function is required to be copyable, and passing a non-copyable request into it violates that.  most of our utility functions capture by std::function now, and FWIW, this is EXACTLY the kind of bug we're trying to catch, where we're making expensive copies of large objects without realizing it (because the std::function is copied).

Ideally we'd move most of our helper functions to std::move_only_function, which would fix that.

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/79346

builds, and is an example of copy working.
It seems good after moving to std::move_only_function (https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/bmcweb/+/79347), and then this can be merged.
Ack.
